claims.text: The degree of surface chemical heterogeneity governs the premelting and melting behavior of HEA nanoparticles.
Locally enhanced short-range order or atomic segregation at the nanoparticle surface lowers local cohesive energies.
Surface short-range order or segregation lowers premelting and complete-melting temperatures relative to uniformly mixed HEA nanoparticles.
Surface short-range order or segregation lowers premelting and complete-melting temperatures relative to bulk HEA materials.
Carbothermal-shock synthesis can produce multielement HEA nanoparticles with a uniform elemental distribution on a support.
The proposed initial particles are equimolar HEA nanoparticles.
Well-dispersed, homogeneously mixed HEA nanoparticles produced by the stated rapid-synthesis methods are typically 10–50 nm in size.
Annealing at 300–500 °C under inert gas will promote surface segregation or short-range ordering.
The proposed annealing treatment can enhance surface heterogeneity without significant particle coalescence.
The experiment compares annealed and identically synthesized unannealed nanoparticles under identical DSC and in-situ TEM heating ramps.
Atomic clusters or short-range order at particle surfaces reflect the extent of surface chemical heterogeneity.
Surface compositional fluctuations and segregation reduce the energy barrier for atomic mobility.
The reduced barrier for surface atomic mobility initiates premelting at lower temperatures.
Annealed nanoparticles with enhanced surface heterogeneity will have statistically significantly lower premelting-onset temperatures than the as-synthesized baseline.
Annealed nanoparticles with enhanced surface heterogeneity will have statistically significantly lower complete-melting temperatures than the as-synthesized baseline.
The predicted surface-heterogeneity effect will be most observable in particles 10–50 nm in size.
Surface-energy effects dominate the thermal behavior of HEA nanoparticles over the roughly 10–50 nm size range.
For much larger particles, the proposed surface-heterogeneity mechanism may weaken or be overridden.
Excessive segregation leading to phase separation may modify or override the proposed mechanism.
The magnitude of the melting-temperature shift may vary with composition, particle-size distribution, and annealing parameters.
